senses.gloss: Public attention focused on one person or issue.
examples: The scandal put the mayor in the *spotlight* for weeks.
She has never been comfortable in the *spotlight*.
The report threw a *spotlight* on conditions at the nursing home.

senses.gloss: Tiny bits of colored candy scattered on ice cream or frosting.
examples: He asked for chocolate *sprinkles* on his cone.
The cupcakes were covered in rainbow *sprinkles*.
There is a jar of *sprinkles* in the baking cabinet.

senses.gloss: A very light, brief fall of rain.
examples: It is just a *sprinkle*, so you do not need an umbrella.
We got a *sprinkle* around noon and nothing after that.
The forecast calls for a few *sprinkles* this evening.

senses.gloss: A chess position in which a player has no legal move and the game ends in a draw.
examples: He was down to one pawn and managed to force a *stalemate*.
The game ended in a *stalemate* on move fifty.
A *stalemate* counts as a draw, not a loss.

senses.gloss: A song that has stayed popular for decades and is played by many performers.
examples: The trio played jazz *standards* all night.
That tune became a *standard* within a few years.
Her album is half originals and half *standards*.

senses.gloss: A flag or banner carried as the emblem of a military unit or a ruler.
examples: The cavalry rode out behind the regiment's *standard*.
Each unit carries its own *standard* in the parade.
The color guard lowered the *standards* at sunset.

senses.gloss: The legal right to bring a case before a court.
examples: The judge ruled that the group had no *standing* to sue.
The case was thrown out for lack of *standing*.
Only a customer of the bank would have *standing* here.

senses.gloss: The length of time something has existed or continued.
examples: They have a dispute of long *standing* over the property line.
It is a tradition of many years' *standing*.
This is a friendship of thirty years' *standing*.

senses.gloss: Something said or written formally and publicly.
examples: The company issued a *statement* denying the charges.
Police released a brief *statement* Tuesday morning.
She read a short *statement* and took no questions.

senses.gloss: Something done or worn in order to express an idea or attitude.
examples: The bright yellow front door makes a *statement*.
Wearing the pin to work was a political *statement*.
Her resignation was meant as a *statement* about the leadership.

senses.gloss: The British pound as a currency.
examples: The contract is priced in *sterling*, not dollars.
*Sterling* fell sharply after the announcement.
He keeps part of his savings in *sterling*.

senses.gloss: A knife with a slim, sharply pointed blade.
examples: The coroner said the wound was made by a *stiletto*.
He carried a *stiletto* in his boot.
The museum case held two old *stilettos* with ivory handles.

senses.gloss: A large decorated sock hung up at Christmas to be filled with small gifts.
examples: The kids hung their *stockings* over the fireplace.
There was an orange in the toe of every *stocking*.
Her *stocking* was full of candy and a new toothbrush.

senses.gloss: A rule or situation that severely limits what someone can do.
examples: The budget put the department in a fiscal *straitjacket*.
He called the new rules a *straitjacket* on small business.
The treaty became a *straitjacket* neither side could escape.

senses.gloss: A very high level, especially of prices or success.
examples: Housing prices downtown have gone into the *stratosphere*.
One song sent her career into the *stratosphere*.
Ticket prices for the final were up in the *stratosphere*.

senses.gloss: Someone who broadcasts video of themselves live online.
examples: He quit his job to be a full-time *streamer*.
Thousands of *streamers* play the game every night.
Her favorite *streamer* goes live at eight.

senses.gloss: A quality or ability that a person or thing is good at.
examples: Patience is her greatest *strength*.
The report lists the program's *strengths* and weaknesses.
Working with kids has always been his *strength*.

senses.gloss: How concentrated a liquid, a drug, or a flavor is.
examples: The pills come in three different *strengths*.
Cut the cleaner to half *strength* before you use it.
I like my coffee at full *strength*.

senses.gloss: A part-time reporter who sends stories to a news organization from a place it does not staff.
examples: The paper pays a *stringer* to cover the state capital.
She started out as a *stringer* for a wire service.
*Stringers* filed the first reports from the border.

senses.gloss: A short physical fight in which people grab and push each other.
examples: Police found signs of a *struggle* in the kitchen.
The gun went off during the *struggle*.
He tore his shirt in the *struggle* with the intruder.

senses.gloss: One of the smaller parts into which something larger is divided.
examples: The county is the largest political *subdivision* in the state.
Each chapter is broken into three *subdivisions*.
The agency is a *subdivision* of the state health department.

senses.gloss: The act of giving in to someone else's power or authority.
examples: The rebels were starved into *submission*.
He nodded in *submission* and said nothing more.
She refused to be bullied into *submission*.

senses.gloss: The real meaning or important content of something, as opposed to its form.
examples: The speech was long on style and short on *substance*.
The *substance* of the complaint is that nobody was told.
There is no *substance* to the rumor.

senses.gloss: A person or thing used in place of another.
examples: There is no *substitute* for hard work.
She uses a sugar *substitute* in her coffee.
Frozen berries make a decent *substitute* in this recipe.

senses.gloss: A player sent onto the field to replace another during a game.
examples: The coach sent in a *substitute* at halftime.
He came on as a *substitute* and scored twice.
Each team may use three *substitutes* per game.

senses.gloss: A second, longer title printed under the main title of a book or article.
examples: The book's *subtitle* explains what it is actually about.
Her article carried the *subtitle* 'A Year on the River'.
Publishers often add a *subtitle* to help sales.

senses.gloss: A small, fine detail or distinction that is easy to miss.
examples: The translation loses the *subtleties* of the original.
He explained the *subtleties* of the tax rule.
There is a *subtlety* here that most readers skip right over.
